title: Modeling human retinoblastoma using embryonic stem cell-derived retinal organoids
protocol: Prepare a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate.
Keep the hESC culture medium ready at 22°C–25°C.
Remove cryopreserved hESC vial from liquid nitrogen storage tank and transfer to 37°C water bath to thaw quickly.
Transfer most of the thawed contents slowly to a 15-mL tube.
Add 5 mL of hESC culture medium drop wise to the tube.
Gently shake the tube to mix the cells.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at 22°C–25°C.
Carefully aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL hESC culture medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632.
Completely aspirate Matrigel from one well of a precoated 6-well plate.
Add the cell suspension into the well immediately.
Place the plate into a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Gently shake to evenly distribute the cells.
Prewarm DPBS and hESC culture medium to 20°C–25°C.
Remove spent medium containing debris from the cells.
Wash the cells once with 1 mL prewarmed DPBS.
Add 2 mL of fresh, prewarmed hESC culture medium without Y-27632 for feeding.
Refresh the culture medium daily until passaging is required.
Monitor cell morphology under an inverted microscope.
Scrape off large differentiated colonies using a P1000 pipette tip.
Proceed to passage when hESC colonies are becoming too large or reaching 60%–80% confluent (approx. 3–5 days).
Prewarm hESC culture medium, DPBS and EDTA Dissociation Buffer to 20°C–25°C.
Prepare a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate and add 2 mL of hESC culture medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632 per well.
Aspirate the spent medium from the hESCs to be passaged.
Rinse the cells with 2 mL DPBS and EDTA solution sequentially.
Add 1 mL of EDTA solution to each well.
Incubate for 2–5 min at 22°C–25°C within the hood.
Remove the EDTA solution carefully without disturbing the attached cell layer.
Use 2 mL of hESC culture medium with 10 μM Y-27632 to wash the colonies off the plate and dissociate cells by gently pipetting up and down three times.
Transfer the desired cell amount per well into Matrigel-coated plates in a ratio of about 1:6–1:10.
Shake the plates back and forth and side to side to distribute the cells evenly.
Incubate the cells for 12 hours to allow maximum attachment.
Remove the culture medium from the cells the next day.
Rinse the cells with 1 ml prewarmed DPBS.
Add 2 ml of prewarmed hESC culture medium without Y-27632 to each well in a 6-well plate.
Repeat daily steps to change the culture medium.
Monitor cell growth and status daily.
Aspirate culture medium when hESC colonies are reaching 60%–80% confluent.
Rinse the cells with 1 mL prewarmed DPBS and TrypLE Select solution sequentially.
Incubate with another 1 mL TrypLE Select solution for 3–5 min at 37°C.
Optional: Pretreat with 10 μM Y-27632 in hESC culture medium for 2 h before single-cell plating to enhance cell survival rate.
Gently pipette up and down the TrypLE Select solution three times using a P1000 pipette tip.
Monitor dissociation under a bright-field microscope to ensure cells are dissociated into single cells.
Transfer the single-cell suspension to a 15-mL centrifuge tube containing 5 mL of hESC culture medium.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend approximately 2 × 10^6 cells in nucleofector solution by mixing 82 μL P3 primary cell solution and 18 μL supplement 1.
Mix resuspended cells with 5 μg of plasmid cocktail, including 2.5 μg of guide-carrying plasmids and 2.5 μg of RB1 targeting vector.
Transfer the mixture into a nucleofection cuvette.
Electroporate cells using program CA-137 on Nucleofector 4D.
Gently transfer electroporated cells into Matrigel-coated plates containing hESC culture medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632.
Culture the plates in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 48 hours.
Treat cells with 2 μg/mL puromycin for about 7 days after electroporation.
Prepare a Matrigel-coated 24-well plate.
After coating, replace Matrigel with 0.5 mL of hESC culture medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632 per well.
Pick surviving clones and prepare them for expanding and further genotyping.
Find cell colonies under the microscope.
Cross-hatch the colony with a smaller-gauge needle to break it into smaller pieces.
Use a P1000 pipette tip to push the colony off the plate and suck it into the pipette.
Transfer the colony pieces into one well of the 24-well plate.
Place the plate into a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Gently shake the plate to evenly distribute the cells.
Extract genomic DNA from individual colonies using DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit according to manufacturer's instructions.
Detect the HR and non-HR allele by PCR using Primer1F, Primer1R, Primer2F, Primer2R, or Primer3F with Primer2R.
Examine the PCR fragments by Sanger sequencing.
Identify potential mutations of RB1 gene by comparing the colony sequence with WT sequence.
Maintain RB1Mut/Mut hESCs routinely as described in steps 1–14 for WT hESCs.
Optionally, remove resistance gene (puro) in RB1-mutated hESCs using the Cre/LoxP system.
Perform western blotting with anti-Rb antibody at 1:1,000 dilutions to analyze the expression of RB protein (pRB) in RB1Mut/Mut clones.
Conduct flow cytometry analysis for pluripotency marker genes (i.e., Oct3/4 or Sox2) in RB1Mut/Mut clones.
Dissociate the clones into single-cell suspension using prewarmed TrypLE Select solution carefully.
Wash the cells twice with PBS and resuspend them in media.
Stain the cells with Alexa Fluor 488/647-conjugated antibodies (1:50) in PEB buffer for 30 min at 4°C.
Filter the stained cells through a 100 μm nylon mesh.
Analyze the fluorescence of the cells by FACSCanto II.
Wash the culture medium with DPBS and aspirate it.
Treat the cells with 0.1 μg/mL colcemid at 37°C for 2 h.
Dissociate the clones into single-cell suspension using prewarmed TrypLE Select solution carefully.
Resuspend and incubate the cells in 0.075 M potassium chloride for 15 min at 37°C.
Fix the cells with 3:1 methanol:acetic acid.
Drop the fixed cells onto slides to spread the chromosomes.
Stain the chromosomes with Giemsa staining solution.
Check the confluency of RB1Mut/Mut hESCs on day 0.
Dissociate cells into single-cell suspension using prewarmed TrypLE Select solution.
Count cell density.
Plate cells at a density of 12,000 live cells per well in 96-well low-attachment V-bottom plates with 100 μL differentiation medium I supplemented with 20 μM Y-27632.
Put the plates on a spiral mixer device and shake for 10 minutes at 60-80 rpm.
Place the plates into a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
On day 6, take out the plate and slightly tilt it.
Use an 8-channel P100 pipette to carefully aspirate the medium from each well.
Quickly add 100 μL fresh differentiation medium I containing 55 ng/mL hBMP4 to each well.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 3 days.
On day 9, carefully remove 50 μL medium from each well.
Change equal volume of fresh differentiation medium I (without hBMP4) back to each well.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 3 additional days.
Gently tap the plate from both sides on day 18 to make aggregates free-floating.
Transfer organoids using a wide-mouth P1000 pipette tip into a 15-mL conical tube.
Let the organoids settle at the bottom of the tube for approximately 1–2 minutes.
Carefully remove the supernatant from the top.
Add 5 mL differentiation medium II to wash the organoids.
Let the organoids settle to the bottom and remove excess differentiation medium II.
Resuspend the organoids with 10 mL differentiation medium II using a 10-mL pipette.
Transfer the resuspended organoids into a low attachment 9-cm Petri dish.
Manually trisect the organoids using a V-Lance Knife under an inverted microscope in a Class II biological hood.
Add 10 mL of additional differentiation medium II to the Petri dish.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 /40% O2 for continued induction.
Refresh the differentiation medium II every 7 days by rotating the dish to gather organoids in the center.
Carefully aspirate media from the surrounding without disturbing organoids using a vacuum aspiration system.
Replace with 20 mL fresh differentiation medium II.
Gently swirl the Petri dish every day to avoid organoids adhering to the bottom.
Take out the dish on day 20.
Remove badly differentiated organoids using a 10-mL pipette.
Separate fused organoids using a V-Lance Knife under the inverted microscope.
Place the dish into the incubator for further culture.
Monitor the state and morphology of organoids in real time using an inverted microscope.
Pipette adhered organoids with the medium to resuspend them.
Remove poorly conditioned organoids using a 10-mL pipette.
Rotate the dish to gather the organoids in the center.
Aspirate the medium from around the organoids carefully using vacuum aspiration system.
Replace aspirated media with fresh medium without disturbing the organoids.
Culture organoids in suspension in a Petri dish.
Change half the medium every 5 days for organoids in suspension culture.
On day 30, remove badly differentiated organoids.
Separate fused organoids under an inverted microscope.
Gently distribute organoids into multiple dishes using a 10-mL pipette.
Ensure no more than 30 organoids per dish.
Return the dishes to a 37°C, 5% CO2 /40% O2 incubator.
Change the medium every 7 days.
Perform media change routinely every 5–7 days as described in step 46.
Gently distribute the organoids into multiple dishes using a 10-mL pipette, with no more than 15 organoids per dish.
Refresh the medium every 5 days as described in step 46.
Gently trisect the larger organoids using a V-Lance Knife under the inverted microscope for long-term culture.
Avoid allowing organoids to grow too large to prevent nutrient deficiency in cells inside the organoids.
Select organoids with obvious tumor-like “primary foci” after day 75.
Slightly transfer selected organoids into a 2-mL tube using a 10-mL pipette.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully.
Wash the organoids three times with 1 mL DPBS.
Add 0.5 mL 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution to fix the organoids at 37°C for 1 hour.
Wash the organoids three times with PBS.
Stain the organoids with Ponceau S solution at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Wash the organoids with NEG-50 Frozen Section Medium.
Carefully embed the organoids into a disposable embedding mold containing NEG-50 Frozen Section Medium.
Place the molds into −80°C refrigerator for 20–30 minutes to freeze the organoids.
Cryosection the frozen organoids at a thickness of 12–16 μm on slides using a cryostat.
Once fixed and embedded, store organoids at −80°C for more than 12 months.
After cryosectioning, subject the sections to immunocytochemistry or storage at −80°C for up to 12 months.
Wash the sections three times for 10 minutes with PBS.
Block and permeabilize the sections in 4% BSA with 0.5% Triton X-100 for 1 hour at 22°C–25°C.
Dilute the primary antibody in PBS with 1% BSA and 0.5% Triton X-100.
Incubate sections with appropriate dilutions (1:100–1:400) of primary antibody at 4°C for 12 hours.
Aspirate the spent blocking buffer from the sections.
Dilute the secondary antibody (1:400) in PBS with 1% BSA and 0.5% Triton X-100.
Incubate sections with secondary antibody dilution in the dark at 22°C–25°C for 1 hour.
Aspirate the secondary antibody dilution from the sections.
Wash sections three times for 10 minutes with PBS.
Add 300 nM DAPI nuclear stain solution and incubate in the dark at 22°C–25°C for 5-10 minutes.
Remove the staining solution and wash sections three times with PBS.
Using absorbent paper, absorb moisture around the sections.
Add 10 μL antifade mounting medium to each section.
Gently cover the cover slips.
Seal edges of coverslips using transparent nail varnish and dry for 3 minutes.
Store slides at 4°C in the dark.
Take out dishes containing organoids during days 30–50.
Collect organoids using a 10-mL pipette and transfer into a 15-mL tube with 1 mL differentiation medium II.
Place the tube on ice for 10 minutes.
Remove supernatant from the top of the tube.
Replace with 1 mL pre-chilled cryopreservation pretreatment solution.
Incubate on ice for 10–15 minutes.
Remove pretreatment solution.
Add pre-chilled organoid cryopreservation medium to resuspend the organoids.
Transfer 200 μL of cryopreservation medium containing 15-20 organoids to a labeled 1.5-mL cryovial.
Directly freeze vials in liquid nitrogen for storage.
Take out stock vials from liquid nitrogen for thawing.
Add 1 mL prewarmed (20°C–25°C) differentiation medium II to thaw frozen human Rb organoids quickly.
Remove supernatant after thawing.
Wash twice with differentiation medium II.
Transfer the organoids to a new Petri dish using a 10-mL pipette.
Add 15 mL of differentiation medium II for post-maintenance culture.
